## Use cases for generative AI in marketing

Generative AI uses a combination of advanced technologies to create, personalize and optimize content and customer interactions. Some common use cases include:

* [Chatbots and customer experience](#2.1)
* [Text generation and image generation](#2.2)
* [Personalization and segmentation](#2.3)
* [Data analysis and predictive analysis](#2.4)
* [Process automation](#2.5)
* [Idea generation](#2.6)

### Chatbots and customer experience

Generative AI enhances customer interaction by providing instant, intelligent responses and support across various touchpoints. This might include an AI chatbot handling potential customer inquiries, providing product information and ushering consumers through a sale—all in natural, intuitive language. AI-driven virtual assistants also guide users through websites, recommend purchases and improve the overall user experience.

For instance, generative AI customer interaction tools might automatically respond to customer reviews and complaints in a brand’s voice, summarizing potential issues for an organization’s customer support team. Generative AI might even automate future discounts or product replacements.

Chatbots and virtual agents trained on an organization’s proprietary data provide round-the-clock assistance and global reach across time zones. Combined with Robotic Process Automation (RPA), they can trigger specific actions, such as initiating a sale or return process, without human intervention. As these generative AI tools “remember” interactions with customers, they can nurture leads over long periods, maintaining a cohesive relationship with an individual consumer. These highly personalized experiences engender loyalty and increase conversion rates.

Generative AI chatbots also collect crucial information for marketers about consumer preferences and behavior. They can analyze this vast and invaluable dataset to make recommendations and improve operations across a business.

### Text generation and image generation

Generative AI revolutionizes the content supply chain from end-to-end by automating and optimizing the creation, distribution and management of marketing content. Applications for AI in content marketing include automated content creation. Through these processes, AI tools generate high-quality blog posts, social media updates and ad copy based on specific keywords, topics and styles.

Generative AI also creates custom images and video tailored to brand aesthetics and campaign needs, enhancing visual content without the need for extensive design resources.

These models also significantly accelerate the creative production process, allowing marketing professionals to rapidly create and test various creative assets, creating fully fledged campaigns in a matter of hours or days.

### Personalization and segmentation

Where traditional AI might have helped marketing professionals segment audiences into broad groups according to purchasing history or taste, generative AI has ushered in an era of micro-segmentation. Micro-segmentation gives organizations the power to market to specific individuals in close to real-time. This type of personalization is a key strength of generative AI, allowing marketers to deliver highly targeted and relevant experiences to consumers at scale across channels.

For instance, generative AI might create customized recipes and meal-planning ideas based on customer grocery orders, or interpret an individual’s feedback to generate product recommendations.

Generative AI also enhances adaptive content, in which websites, emails and mobile apps adjust their displays in real-time based on individual user interactions and data, creating the most relevant possible experience for consumers. An AI tool trained on a brand’s specific messaging can craft individual creative assets for small audience segments, helping ensure marketing communications resonate as effectively as possible with diverse customer groups.

### Data analysis and predictive analytics

Generative AI excels at analyzing vast amounts of data to uncover customer insights and predict future trends, enabling data-driven decision-making. This might include market research analysis, a process through which AI algorithms interpret market data or competitor pricing to identify future consumer behavior and broader industry dynamics.

Other generative AI tools might use customer data to surface and target particularly relevant audiences. Using the technology, organizations can quickly and efficiently identify the best possible leads and predict future trends, helping marketers plan proactive campaigns and optimize their resources.

### Process automation

Generative AI streamlines marketing processes using [automation](https://www.ibm.com/topics/automation). By automating repetitive and time-consuming tasks, organizations can achieve increased efficiency and productivity. Some AI-powered tools can automate various marketing workflows such as social media posting or email sequencing, freeing up human resources for more strategic initiatives. Some are used to manage specific marketing campaigns, monitor campaign data and optimize the delivery of advertisements or communications based on performance.

Generative AI is also used to translate content from one language to another, or convert files into several formats, streamlining marketing departments’ day-to-day operations and increasing a brand's reach.

The technology can also optimize the creative production process. Using generative AI, marketing departments can rapidly generate dozens of versions of a piece of content and then A/B test that content to automatically determine the most effective variation of an ad.

### Idea generation

Generative AI can stimulate creativity and innovation by generating new ideas and content variations. Marketing departments might use generative AI to suggest search engine optimization (SEO) headlines or topics based on current trends and audience interests.

For example, according to the consultancy McKinsey, Kellogg’s uses AI technologies to scan viral recipes that incorporate breakfast cereal. Generative AI then uses that data to create creative assets and social media posts.4 During the ideation process, generative AI can also be used to suggest options for logos or advertisements, providing a vast trove of ideas for marketing departments to choose from and refine.

## Benefits of generative AI in marketing

Generative AI offers various ways to optimize business processes and increase [customer engagement](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/customer-engagement), transforming the scale at which marketing departments communicate with and learn from consumers. Some key advantages to using generative AI in marketing include:

* [Increased efficiency through automation](#3.1)
* [Hyper-personalized marketing](#3.2)
* [Scaleability](#3.3)
* [Cost-effectiveness](#3.4)
* [Data-driven decision-making](#3.5)
* [Improved customer experience](#3.6)
* [Real-time adaption](#3.7)

Increased efficiency through automation  

Generative AI automates the creation of content such as social media posts and ad copy, significantly reducing the time and effort required from marketing teams. AI-powered [virtual agents](https://www.ibm.com/topics/virtual-agent) or chatbots communicating in natural language also provide constant, 24-hour customer support with minimal human intervention.

Hyper-personalized marketing  

Generative AI delivers personalized messages, recommendations and offers based on individual customer data and behavior. This enhances the relevance and impact of marketing efforts and increases brand awareness.

Scalability  

Generative AI easily handles large volumes of customer interactions or content creation needs, accommodating growing audiences. It also quickly converts content in multiple languages or formats, helping organizations reach and engage consumers on a global scale.

Cost-effectiveness  

Used in marketing departments, generative AI optimizes resources, freeing up human workers for valuable and creative tasks. It also lowers the cost of experimentation and innovation, rapidly generating multiple variations of content such as ads or blog posts to identify the most effective strategies.

Data-driven decision-making  

AI models interpret, analyze and summarize vast amounts of data to uncover insights into customer behavior, market trends and campaign performance. They also forecast future trends and customer needs, helping marketers to anticipate and respond proactively.

Improved customer experience  

AI marketing tools assist with content generation, creating more [engaging experiences for customers](https://www.ibm.com/topics/customer-experience) and increasing conversion rates. Generative AI across multiple platforms also creates consistent, yet unique, brand messaging across multiple channels and touchpoints.

Real-time adaption  

Generative AI allows organizations to quickly respond to customer feedback and interactions, refining campaigns for better outcomes.

## Steps to implementing generative AI in marketing

While every generative AI implementation is dependent on an organization’s capacity and goals, some common steps to implement generative AI for marketing include:

1. [Defining customer experience goals](#4.1)
2. [Collecting and analyzing data](#4.2)
3. [Choosing generative AI tools](#4.3)
4. [Integrating and deploying generative AI](#4.4)
5. [Monitoring and improving generative AI](#4.5)

### 1. Defining customer experience goals

Typically, decision-makers spend significant time outlining their organization’s goals before designing an AI implementation. This might include auditing existing processes that might benefit from enhancement, identifying workflows that might benefit from generative AI and outlining the wanted customer experience.

### 2. Collecting and analyzing data

During this phase, an organization typically gathers data from various customer touchpoints to understand their preferences, behavior and data points. A business might also collect and clean internal proprietary data, or engage trusted third-party data to create a cohesive dataset on which to train an AI.

### 3. Choosing generative AI tools

Depending on the scope of the AI implementation, an organization might decide on a prebuilt tool or identify what kind of model it will use to train a bespoke AI during this phase. Regardless of how customized the eventual solution will be, organizations generally research options thoroughly before coming to a decision.

### 4. Integrating and deploying generative AI

Integrations might take as little as a few weeks or a year. Large-scale AI transformations might require additional infrastructure and talent, while prebuilt off-the-shelf models might simply dictate that marketing departments input datasets they’ve previously identified. During the training and tuning period, the AI tool learns from third-party and internal data to function more effectively.

### 5. Monitoring and improving generative AI

Typically, an organization consistently reviews its generative AI tools to identify areas for improvement and continuously feeds the AI new data to improve accuracy.

## Best practices when implementing generative AI in marketing

While the use of generative AI offers numerous advantages for marketing departments, it also presents some challenges organizations typically navigate to effectively implement and benefit from the technology. Some of those challenges and potential solutions include:

* [Data quality and availability](#6.1)
* [Data privacy and user trust](#6.2)
* [Quality control and consistency across AI models and outputs](#6.3)

### Data quality and availability

Generative AI models require a huge amount of high-quality data to function effectively. Inaccurate data or data with bias can lead to poor performance and unreliable outputs. Also, gathering and managing the necessary data can be time-consuming and costly, especially for smaller businesses with limited resources. Organizations embarking on a generative AI project might hire additional data scientists and data engineers to help ensure the quality and consistency of a training corpus or engage a trusted third party with vetted data practices.

### Data privacy and user trust

Using customer data for AI-driven personalization and content creation typically requires organizations to keep a close eye on [data privacy](https://www.ibm.com/topics/data-privacy) rules and regulations. As mishandling data can lead to compliance issues and a loss of consumer trust, an organization might need to invest in advanced security infrastructure. Successful generative AI solutions are typically transparent and explainable, meaning the business designing the AI has clear documentation about how it was trained and tuned. Additionally, an organization using proprietary or user data might carefully design the AI tools with the customer’s level of comfort in mind, helping ensure customer experience solutions don’t appear invasive.

### Quality control and consistency across AI models and outputs

Ensuring that AI-generated content meets brand standards and maintains a consistent voice can be challenging. Choosing the right model and thoroughly auditing training data can be time-consuming. In the initial planning phase, an organization typically researches specific foundation models extensively, ensuring the basis of its AI solutions is the most appropriate to deploy for a specific use case. To ensure consistency over the long term, organizations typically monitor a model continuously to detect and correct errors. They might also feed a model more data to make sure it’s up-to-date.

## What Is GenAI and Why Does It Matter for Marketers?

*GenAI* refers to a type of artificial intelligence that is capable of creating new content based on the input it receives. Unlike traditional forms of automation that rely on rigid programming, GenAI dynamically produces unique text, images, videos, and audio that often resemble human creativity. GenAI can discover patterns and structures in large datasets to personalize its outputs.

ChatGPT, DALL·E, and Jasper AI are already helping marketers create interesting blog posts, designs, and video scripts with minimal effort. These tools can take simple prompts and turn them into personalized content, saving marketers hours of manual work.

## Why Is GenAI a Game-Changer for Modern Marketers?

GenAI is a game-changer because it can deliver the following benefits to modern marketers:

* personalization at scale—GenAI can produce personalized email campaigns, product descriptions, and ads that are tailored to individual customers’ preferences.
* dynamic content creation—Brands can refresh their content at high speed—from interactive visuals to social-media posts—without suffering creative burnout.
* greater efficiency—GenAI can automate mundane tasks such as creating captions or designing ads, freeing up time that marketers can dedicate to strategic planning and innovation.

Think about creating hundreds of variants of product descriptions in mere minutes or generating social-media content for an entire month based on just a couple of prompts. This is the level of efficiency that GenAI makes possible.

### A Basic Example of a Workflow

Let’s consider a basic example of a GenAI workflow, as follows:

* Input: A prompt such as, “Write a product description for a smartwatch targeting fitness enthusiasts.”
* Processing: The AI searches its database for relevant patterns and examples.
* Output: A polished, optimized product description that is ready to publish, as shown in Figure 1.

## Personalization at Scale: The AI Superpower

Imagine opening an email message that seems to be written just for you. It has a catchy subject line, the content is highly relevant to your needs, and even the product suggestions seem to fit perfectly. This is the magic of GenAI in operation, empowering marketers to create hyper-personalized content for everything from email campaigns and social media to ecommerce sites. Many brands [partner with growth marketing agencies](https://azariangrowthagency.com/ "partner with growth marketing agencies") for better results because they can ace the creation of these kinds of content.

GenAI bases its personalization on a variety of data, including the user’s browsing history, past purchases, and even social-media behaviors. A good example is Stitch Fix, a brand that analyzes customers’ preferences and uses AI to suggest outfits with matching colors and styles that fit seasonal trends, as shown in Figure 2.

Image source: [Stitchfix Newsroom](https://newsroom.stitchfix.com/blog/how-were-revolutionizing-personal-styling-with-generative-ai/ "Stitchfix Newsroom")

Personalizing content actually makes users feel seen, improves user engagement, and boosts sales. According to recent studies, AI-powered, personalized email messages boast [29% higher](https://www.experianplc.com/newsroom/press-releases/2014/experian-marketing-services-study-finds-personalized-emails-generate-six "29% higher") open rates and 41% higher click-through rates. Imagine the boost to your campaigns when each message has the feeling of being curated for its recipient.

Why does personalization matter? You can generate personalized content for the following:

* email campaigns—GenAI autogenerates subject lines, body text, and calls to action (CTAs) according to individual preferences for better engagement.
* social media—Create posts that target the sentiments of particular segments of the audience to improve reach and engagement.
* ecommerce—Generate dynamic product recommendations and personalized landing pages to enhance the shopping experience.

Personalization at scale is about making every customer interaction meaningful, and GenAI is the transformational engine that drives personalization.

## Rethinking Content Creation: Faster, Smarter, Better

Create content with GenAI and eliminate the painful process of manual content creation. Whether you’re crafting a blog post, writing product descriptions, or generating ad copy, you can generate all of this content with speed and precision using AI tools. There’s no more staring at a blank page. Instead, in mere seconds, GenAI can turn an indistinguishable prompt into a fully formed piece. Today, many brands such as Coca-Cola, shown in Figure 3, Heinz, and BMW are using GenAI to create video ads and build interactive content.

GenAI can analyze trends and audience preferences and use historical data to create stunning visuals and engaging scripts. In fact, many brands are already automating a large portion of their content-creation pipeline, freeing up their teams to work on strategy rather than production.

### Popular Generative AI Tools for Content Creation

In Table 1, take a quick peek at some of the most popular GenAI tools for content creation.

Table 1—GenAI tools for content creation


| Tool | Capabilities | Best for Creating |
| ChatGPT | Conversational text generation, idea brainstorming | Blog posts, customer-support scripts |
| DALL·E | AI-generated images, based on text descriptions | Visual content for social media |
| Jasper AI | Marketing-focused, content-creation tools | Ad copy, email-message text |
| Runway | Video editing and generation with AI | Video ads |
| Copy.ai | Quick generation of product descriptions and ad copy | Ecommerce product pages |

Practical applications of GenAI include the following:

* blog posts—GenAI can create content with search-engine optimization (SEO) in mind, saving time during research and writing.
* product descriptions—Generate engaging, keyword-rich descriptions of hundreds of items in minutes.
* ad campaigns—These tools include Jasper AI and Copy.ai, which write high-quality ad copy that is suitable for the tone of your brand.
* video ads—With Runway, GenAI converts concepts into completed, polished videos with no need for heavy editing.

## Improving Ecommerce with GenAI

Generative AI is driving complete change in ecommerce by offering personalized shopping experiences that customers love. From virtual try-ons to AI-generated product images, this innovative technology is raising the game for how shoppers are interacting with brands online.

Designing an ecommerce experience is no longer just about selling a product—it’s about delivering a personalized experience that is easy and seamless to use.

### Real-World Example: Personalized Shopping Experiences in Action

Sephora has jumped on the AI bandwagon, thanks to its Virtual Artist feature, shown in Figure 4. This AI-powered tool lets customers try on makeup products virtually by uploading selfies. The AI changes everything from lipsticks to eyeshadows to fit each user’s unique facial structure and skin tone.

Image source: [Sephora]( https://www.sephora.sg/pages/virtual-artist?srsltid=AfmBOoqp3nVCTbb0G-PioqqRbEmqYuQIrIw75A_fiF32LRpiT-t6BS1_ "Sephora")

But Sephora didn’t stop there. It mixed virtual try-ons with AI-generated product recommendations that are based on customers’ browsing habits and past purchases.

The result:

* A [30% increase](https://www.theglimpsegroup.com/case-studies/sephora-increases-online-make-up-sales-by-35-percent-with-virtual-try-on-experience "30% increase") in conversion rate
* A [2.5x increase](https://www.techrepublic.com/article/how-sephora-is-leveraging-ar-and-ai-to-transform-retail-and-help-customers-buy-cosmetics/ "2.5x increase") in the time shoppers spent on the site after the implementation of AI.
* A significant reduction in returns, with customers being more assured of their purchasing decisions.

### Key Benefits of Generative AI for Ecommerce

For ecommerce applications, GenAI offers the following benefits:

* personalized recommendations—AI scans the data and suggests only products relating to the individual customer’s preferences. This encourages upselling and cross-selling opportunities.
* personalized landing pages—Engaging, AI-crafted pages match very specific customer needs, increasing the chances of conversion.
* virtual try-ons—Customers can try on items—from cosmetics to clothes—virtually, increasing their confidence when purchasing.
* AI-generated visuals—Compositing realistic product images for products that haven’t yet been photographed accelerates time to market.
* improved inventory management—AI can forecast demand based on trends and sales patterns, helping retailers stock more efficiently.

### The Numbers Don’t Lie

GenAI for ecommerce is a game-changer. AI-powered recommendations drive [30% of Amazon’s revenue](https://www.forbes.com/sites/petercohan/2024/07/01/amazon-stock-up-30-but-huge-ai-bet-may-not-restore-27-growth/ "30% of Amazon's revenue"), underlining the strong potential of this technology. Adding GenAI to your ecommerce strategy helps personalize customers’ shopping experience, keeping operations lean, and ultimately, improving profit margins. From providing customers precisely what they need to meeting them where they are, AI is helping ecommerce platforms rewrite the future of online shopping.

Pro Tip: Pair GenAI with an infographic that shows how AI impacts various stages of the ecommerce customer journey—all the way from browsing to checkout.

## Revolutionizing Paid Ads with GenAI

Generative AI can automate copywriting and design visuals for paid ads and optimize campaigns in real time. Tools such as AdCreative.ai leverage large volumes of data to create resonant, data-driven ads that improve efficiency and effectiveness for target audiences.

GenAI can transform paid ads in the following ways:

* ad-copy generation—AI generates attention-grabbing headlines and apt descriptions that are targeted toward certain groups.
* visual design—AI designs visually appealing graphics, each one optimized for everything from social media to display networks.
* campaign optimization—AI continuously monitors performance metrics, readjusting targeting and bidding strategies with the goal of maximizing return on investment (ROI).

### Real-World Example: Häagen-Dazs AI-Optimized Campaign

Häagen-Dazs had difficulty promoting a variety of their products, shown in Figure 5, in the fiercely competitive Spanish market.

Image source: [AdCreative.ai]( https://www.adcreative.ai/post/how-ad-creative-ai-is-shaping-the-future-of-advertising-for-enterprises "AdCreative.ai")

In partnership with AdCreative.ai, Häagen-Dazs generated more than [150 variations](https://www.adcreative.ai/post/revolutionizing-enterprise-advertising-how-ai-reduces-workload-and-accelerates-results "150 variations") of their creatives for each product in minutes. This approach ultimately led to a massive increase in engagement, with over 11,000 **Get Directions** clicks in April 2023, at a $1.70 decrease in cost per mille (CPM) due to increases click-through rates and better ad scores.

### Benefits of Generative AI in Paid Advertising

GenAI offers the following benefits for paid advertising:

* time efficiency—Fast creation of ad creatives is accelerating the speed at which campaigns can go live.
* data-driven insights—AI employs analytics to create content that appeals to audience preferences.
* value proposition’s improved ROI—Continuous optimization means better performance and cost savings.
* scalability—AI can produce multiple ad variations that facilitate A/B testing and audience segmentation.

## Challenges and Ethical Considerations

GenAI opens exciting, new avenues in digital marketing. However, it also has challenges relating to biases in AI-generated content, copyright issues, and concerns about the privacy of users’ data. Thus, marketers must proceed with caution, making sure that their usage of this technology is effective and, at the same time, ethical.

Possible risks of GenAI include the following:

* AI content bias—If the data the models are learning from contains any kind of bias or error, the generated content also contains stereotypes or inaccuracies.
* copyright concerns—AI tools might inadvertently create outputs that closely resemble other works, raising potential copyright disputes.
* overreliance on automation—Overindulgence in the use of GenAI can lead to generalized outputs and leave no room for human imagination and subtlety.
* privacy issues—According to Pew Research, documentation shows that 60% of consumers fear that the use of GenAI for personal-marketing campaigns could make them prone to compromising their privacy.

### Best Practices for Responsible Use

Marketers can reduce these risks through the following practices, which ensure the responsible use of GenAI:

* human oversight—Manually vet AI-generated content for veracity, equity, and consistency with your brand’s voice.
* sourcing data ethically—Datasets should be representative, diverse, and free from bias encoding.
* transparency—Be open with your audience regarding the use and role of GenAI so you can develop users’ trust and achieve accountability.
* respecting copyrights—Make sure AI-generated content is original or, if not, is appropriately credited to avoid infringement and legal disputes.
* balancing AI with human creativity—Balance AI efficiency with human creativity to ensure authenticity and originality.

### Ethical Tips for Marketers

The following guidelines foster the ethical user of GenAI for marketers:

* Establish guiding principles for AI-generated content that align with company values.
* Use GenAI to augment rather than replace human creativity.
* Periodically audit the AI outputs to check for biases or inaccuracies.
* Educate your team about the limitations of AI and its ethical implications.

GenAI is only as valuable as the responsibility with which you use it. “The key to making AI work for you, *not* against you,” says Grannis, “is finding that balance with ethical practices an audience can trust.”

Pro Tip: For easy visualization, provide an infographic reflecting common AI risks and their corresponding solutions.

## The Future of GenAI in Digital Marketing

Within five years, GenAI will transform marketing in ways that we can only just begin to imagine. Through further development, GenAI will go beyond the creation of content to entirely new dimensions of personalization, creativity, and engagement.

### What Is on the Horizon?

The future of GenAI in digital marketing will advance the following applications of GenAI:

* AI-powered metaverse advertising—GenAI will make ad experiences in the metaverse more immersive by tailoring virtual environments for each user. Imagine customers walking into a 3D virtual store that is built just for them.
* fully automated content pipelines—From ideation through publishing, AI could handle the full content lifecycle, freeing marketers to focus their work on strategy and innovation.
* real-time personalization—GenAI can analyze user behaviors in real time and immediately adjust content to reflect their changing tastes and preferences.
* AI-generated influencers—AI-powered virtual influencers are already on the rise. These virtual personas will be able to entertain audiences 24/7, with none of the logistical headaches of their human counterparts.

### Emerging Trends

Trends in GenAI that are currently emerging include the following:

* More applications of AI in visual storytelling such as realistic video generation on demand.
* Integration of AI-powered tools into wearables and Internet of Things (IoT) devices to offer hyper-targeted marketing.
* Personalization of experiences via advancements in natural-language generation to create interactive, conversational exchanges with human-feeling AI-powered chatbots.

### Why Marketers Should Love GenAI

GenAI is more than a trend. It’s the future of marketing. The brands that get in, adopt, and start experimenting with these tools now will set the bar for innovation tomorrow. GenAI can upscale creativity, automate processes, and deliver results that we’ve never seen before—but only if marketers can dream big possibilities.

Call to Action: Begin incorporating GenAI in small ways by introducing it into workflows. Feel its power, measure its impact, and build expertise. These tools are here, so now is the time to begin exploring how they could revolutionize marketing. The future of AI-driven digital marketing holds endless possibilities. Will you be a part of this future?

## Conclusion: Join the GenAI Revolution

GenAI is *not* something from a futuristic movie plot, but is very much here and now and is redefining how marketers get in front of audiences, create content, and drive results. From personalized shopping experiences to AI-optimized ads, the possibilities of GenAI are endless.

However, with great power comes great responsibility. The opportunities are endless, and the time to begin exploring them is now. Test, innovate, and find ways to weave GenAI into your strategy. Whether they’re crafting hyper-personalized email messages or are on the bleeding edge of AI-driven metaverse ads, the brands that are taking action today will define the marketing landscape of tomorrow. GenAI is absolutely *not* a flash in the pan—it’s the next big wave. The question now is how you can use GenAI to shape your brand’s future.

# AI Will Shape the Future of Marketing

AI presents marketers with a variety of opportunities to personalize customer experiences and to build their technological skills.

* [Melissa Russell](/author/melissa-russell/)

  Melissa Russell is an award-winning journalist and editor living in the Boston area. She has written for many news outlets as well as for websites, trade publications and other platforms.

[Blog](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/category/blog/)

Apr 14, 2025

14 minute read

On this page

Did you ever wonder how Spotify compiles its daily mix of tunes you’d like to hear? Or how Netflix makes recommendations of films you’re sure to enjoy?

Thank the marketing professionals who are using artificial intelligence to zero in on what consumers most want to see, hear, read, and purchase.

From chatbots to social media management to full-scale marketing campaigns and automation, artificial intelligence is changing the way marketers do their jobs. Routine tasks like writing copy, mining consumer data, and creating visuals that once took hours can now be done in minutes.

Businesses should view AI as an opportunity to provide more customized and relevant marketing experiences for their customers and ultimately drive their business forward.

### Meet Our Expert

[Learn more about Christina](/faculty/christina-inge/)

[Christina Inge](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/faculty/christina-inge/), author of “Marketing Analytics: A Comprehensive Guide and Marketing Metrics,” and instructor at the Harvard Division of Continuing Education’s Professional & Executive Development, calls AI both a challenge and an opportunity for those in marketing.

“There is a saying going around now — and it is very true— that your job will not be taken by AI,” says Inge. “It will be taken by a person who knows how to use AI. So, it is very important for marketers to know how to use AI.”

At present, many marketers are underutilizing AI, but the impact of AI in marketing is already transforming the business landscape, helping leaders make data-informed decisions with greater efficiency and accuracy. From predictive insights to immersive experiences, AI is redefining how marketers handle repetitive tasks, make decisions, and connect with customers.

While there are challenges ahead, the industry is changing, and professionals who want to future-proof their careers must master the use of AI.

## The Current State of AI in Marketing

How will AI impact marketing? AI platforms like HubSpot, Constant Contact, Mailchimp, and ActiveCampaign are already being used by marketers to automate tasks and optimize campaigns.

The [2024 State of Marketing AI Report](https://www.marketingaiinstitute.com/hubfs/The%202024%20State%20of%20Marketing%20AI%20Report%20from%20Marketing%20AI%20Institute%20and%20Drift.pdf) from the Marketing AI Institute says AI adoption is accelerating among marketing professionals, with many saying they use AI in digital tools in their daily workflows and “couldn’t live without AI.”

### How marketers use AI tools

* Reducing time spent on repetitive, data-driven tasks like content marketing, email, social media, or customer relationship management
* Gaining more actionable insights from data
* Accelerating revenue growth
* Unlocking greater value from marketing technologies

According to Inge, marketers are using AI for market research, creating reports about the state of an industry or sector, and demonstrating ideas that can be later executed on.

“It really makes your work easier to be able to sketch something out through AI, show it to your client or boss and then have them give feedback on that, versus creating multiple iterations of the same product,” she said. “It’s a real efficiency driver.”

While use of AI technology is clearly on the rise, there are still challenges to full AI adoption, including the lack of:

* education and training
* awareness or understanding
* strategy
* talent with the right skill sets
* investment, both of time and of financial resources

“Right now, the vast majority of marketers are underutilizing AI. I’ll be honest with you; it will make your job a lot easier. Let’s take advantage of that,” Inge says.

## Emerging AI Trends in Marketing

When marketers develop strategies to figure out what consumers want, they traditionally have examined demographic trends and surveys, plus intuition and assumptions based on past performance. AI has changed that approach dramatically.

Algorithms are now analyzing customer interactions in real time, predicting consumer behavior and personalizing content. Recommendation engines analyze browsing history and purchase patterns to suggest products that specific consumers might be interested in. Marketers who once reacted to consumer behavior can now predict it and create personalized campaigns.

### AI marketing trends

**Advanced data analytics** AI can collect, process, and analyze easily searchable information like names, purchase histories, and website interactions, but can also mine unstructured data such as images, videos, and social media posts to gain insights about consumer preferences, brand perception, and shopping trends.

**Hyper-personalization** AI’s predictive power allows businesses to anticipate customer preferences based on behavior and customize marketing to individual needs and craft experiences that make customers feel seen and valued.

**Chatbots and virtual assistants** Advanced chatbots and assistants can handle customer queries, recommend products, and complete transactions in real time. By identifying products in images, virtual assistants can personalize shopping experiences by informing customers about similar items they might like.

AI is transforming how companies engage with their audiences, making marketing more intelligent, data-driven, and responsive to individual customer needs.

## AI Marketing Tools Spotlight

AI tools are empowering marketers to make faster, more informed decisions. Tools like Adobe Sensei and Google Marketing Platform allow marketers to streamline their workflow by integrating data analysis, campaign management, and predictive modeling into a single interface.

“I’m using a tool called Blaze that helps you schedule your social media posts. It will give you a whole week or month’s content calendar with the click of a few buttons. I’m also really enjoying using AI to create short explainer videos,” says Inge.

* [ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/) Builds chatbots for e-commerce sites and social media platforms, generates leads and personalized email campaigns based on consumer behavior and interests, creates social media campaigns, assists customers through purchasing processes, helps to brainstorm ideas, formulate strategies, and produce content.
* [Copilot for Microsoft](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/maximize-impact?msockid=32b2238310ad6dad2e36319511aa6c9f) Generates ideas, drafts marketing plans and blogs, and creates social media posts.
* [Gemini for Google Workspace](https://workspace.google.com/solutions/ai/marketing/) Crafts messaging, evaluates large amounts of information, summarizes documents, and automates regular tasks.
* [Jasper AI](https://www.jasper.ai/state-of-ai-marketing-2025) Generates content and data analysis, analytics, and insights.
* [HubSpot](https://www.hubspot.com/startups/ai-insights-for-marketers?irclickid=Wa%3ATwCWr7xyKWsb2KKXrE3p0Uks1OXXNIz1yUU0&irgwc=1&mpid=2003851&utm_id=am2003851&utm_medium=am&utm_source=am2003851&utm_campaign=amcid_Wa%3ATwCWr7xyKWsb2KKXrE3p0Uks1OXXNIz1yUU0_irpid_2003851) Attracts leads through ad campaigns and landing pages, manages social media accounts, personalizes marketing content, and tracks marketing progress.
* [Optmyzr](https://www.optmyzr.com/) Offers pay-per-click management.
* [Synthesia](https://www.synthesia.io/marketing) Creates video, personalizes campaigns, and creates training content.

[Explore all Professional & Executive Development programs in marketing](/find-a-program/?live_global[refinementList][subject_areas][0]=Marketing)

## Personalization At Scale

Today’s consumers expect brand interactions to feel customized to their needs, and AI can help make that possible.

AI enables marketing professionals to tailor campaigns by analyzing customer behavior and preferences, delivering highly personalized experiences from product recommendations to targeted advertisements.

Soon, personalization will become even more tailored to the individual, allowing businesses to customize their content to their audience’s needs with ever-growing accuracy.

### Data-driven customer journeys

Imagine knowing exactly who will open an email, click through, and make a purchase. Through predictive analytics, natural language processing, machine learning, and programmatic advertising, AI allows marketers to process and analyze huge amounts of consumer data quickly. I can also extract insights about consumer preferences, motivations, and purchasing behavior, as well as broader trends.

Businesses are gaining deeper insights into their customers through social media, reviews, and customer service interactions, and this understanding allows brands to tailor messaging to inspire greater customer loyalty.

### Hyper-targeted campaigns

In an age of information overload, AI is revolutionizing the way products are recommended to consumers.

Marketers can cut through the noise to deliver hyper-targeted campaigns that provide the right message to the right audience at the right time. Industries like health care, education, and entertainment can deliver individualized product recommendations and dynamic email content that enhance customer engagement, as well as chatbots for personalized conversations tailored to unique needs and preferences.

By understanding a user’s preferences and behavior, AI algorithms recommend products and relevant content, creating a seamless, personalized consumer experience.

Think of Netflix, which collects vast amounts of data on its customers, such as viewing history and search inquiries. By analyzing this data, Netflix’s AI algorithms generate recommendations tailored to personal preferences.

Amazon is another example: by analyzing purchase history, browsing behavior, and demographic information, the company’s recommendation engine delivers tailored product suggestions that are relevant to its users.

## AI Opportunities and Challenges

While AI can make marketing tasks more efficient and productive, Inge points out that it is already impacting individual roles such as copywriting and design.

“How do we nurture new talent if entry-level tasks become automated?” she says. “While there are substantial opportunities, there are also important challenges that need to be navigated to ensure responsible and ethical use of the technology.”

**Opportunities**

* Increased efficiency and productivity
* Enhanced [innovation](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/blog/what-is-innovation/) and creativity
* Automation and business growth
* Greater return on investment
* Stronger customer relationships
* Improved brand loyalty

**Challenges**

* The rapid pace of AI development and the potential to fall behind
* Over reliance on automation
* Misuse and abuse of AI, such as deep-fakes and copyright infringement
* Privacy and security threats
* Lack of resources and knowledge to fully leverage AI

Inge highlights the continued importance of nurturing future talent, bringing new professionals into the marketing industry, and seeking opportunities to boost what individuals offer, too.

“I worry about how we’re going to bring future marketers into the field because what it replaces the best is that individual contributor,” says Inge. “I got my start in marketing doing some basic work like designing email newsletters. Where’s that all going to come from?”

## Predictive Analytics and Forecasting

Predictive models are essential tools for marketers, enabling hyper-targeted strategies and personalized customer experiences. The models use machine learning and statistics to extrapolate historical data and forecast future events, allowing marketers to analyze consumer behavior and market trends to inform campaigns and strategies and stay ahead of the competition.

Businesses can use AI to refine audience segmentation and identify emerging opportunities by: quickly analyzing vast amounts of data to gain deeper insights into consumer behavior; gaining more precise and actionable data beyond broad demographics; and predicting emerging trends and adjusting messages in real time.

### Examples in action

Lead scoring helps businesses prioritize their potential customers based on the likelihood they will make a sale. By assigning a score to each lead, companies rank them and focus on those that are most likely to result in a successful sale.

AI can help improve lead scoring accuracy by analyzing audience engagement, demographics, and behavior. Machine learning helps marketers predict which leads to prioritize, improving strategy efficiency.

### Lead scoring examples

* **Social media-based lead scoring:** Data gleaned from social media engagement
* **Webpage-based lead scoring:** Examining how users interact with a company website
* **Event-based lead scoring:** Considers user participation in events
* **Predictive lead scoring:** Uses AI and machine learning to forecast the likelihood of lead conversion
* **Dynamic scoring models:** Uses machine learning to create models that adapt to changing behavior

Demand forecasting integrates historical sales data, market trends, and consumer buying patterns to help both large corporations and small businesses anticipate demand, manage inventory, optimize supply chain operations, and avoid overstocking.

### Strategic Impact

AI provides real-time insights into how customers behave all across the sales process, from initial engagement to their final purchase.

The instant feedback allows marketers to adjust campaigns, messaging, and consumer recommendations on the spot, based on their up-to-the-minute behavior, ensuring that businesses can take advantage of opportunities as they present themselves.

By leveraging real-time data, businesses can make faster and more informed decisions to stay ahead of the competition.

## AI-Driven Content Creation

AI is changing the way companies create blog posts, social media messaging, and ad campaigns. Marketers can input specific instructions into ChatGPT or other generative AI models, and in seconds, have AI-generated scripts, articles, and product descriptions specific to their brand voice and audience requirements.

AI is also being used by some marketers to generate images and videos, allowing them to scale every piece of a marketing campaign to specific audience segments and remain competitive in the digital marketplace.

## Generative AI for Marketing

When ChatGPT arrived on the scene in 2022, it garnered headlines and introduced the world to Generative AI innovation.

Using advanced machine learning models, generative AI takes in huge amounts of raw, unstructured and unlabeled data culled from the internet or other source, and performs millions of “fill-in-the-blank” exercises, trying to predict the next element in a sequence.

It fine tunes the material for accuracy and relevance and then uses that information to create original content including text, video and audio with broad applications.

Using generative AI for content creation allows marketers to accomplish more in less time, from creating social media posts and entertainment, turning images into memes of trending topics on Tik Tok, creating stickers for Instagram, responding to queries via a chatbot, providing professional development and recruitment support on LinkedIn, and brainstorming videos for YouTube.

### Human & AI collaboration

Brands can achieve a balance between AI-generated content and human oversight by:

* **Focusing on personalization** Rather than relying on demographics, companies can tailor experiences to individual customers. For example, the beauty brand Sephora uses AI-powered chatbots to answer customer questions and make personalized beauty recommendations. Healthcare companies are using generative AI to develop personalized treatment plans and improve patient care.
* **Being transparent** Disclose the involvement of AI in content creation and allow users to make informed decisions about the content they are consuming.
* **Upholding ethical standards** Maintain trust by establishing accountability frameworks to ensure content aligns with the organization’s [ethical standards](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/blog/what-is-ethical-leadership-and-why-is-it-important/).
* **Engaging with audiences** Use real user stories and testimonials and inject personality and voice to create more engaging and authentic interactions.

### Future possibilities

As AI continues to evolve, its influence in marketing will deepen. From data analysis to creative content generation, businesses will be able to use data-driven decision-making to personalize marketing campaigns.

This personalization will expand beyond e-commerce and entertainment and organizations should be prepared to address challenges posed by algorithm bias and data privacy concerns.

## Ethical Considerations

To ensure AI is used responsibly and protects users’ rights and privacy, companies will need to establish clear policies and guidelines.

According to the World Economic Forum, legislative bodies around the world have passed AI-related laws, demonstrating the concern over AI’s growing influence — particularly over algorithm bias and data privacy. There is also concern that AI will eliminate certain jobs in marketing, particularly entry-level jobs that focus on basic content creation.

Inge also notes the negative environmental impact due to the technology’s energy consumption, and the importance of mitigating these impacts.

### Data privacy

One key ethical concern about the growing use of AI in marketing is data privacy. Sophisticated AI systems rely on vast amounts of consumer data to personalize user experience, but there is growing concern about how this data is collected, used and potentially misused.

“All of these AI companies are using anything they find on the web to train their AI to get better and better, but in many cases, they’re using people’s photos and text without permission,” Inge says. “I think some kind of licensing deal, like what we had with streaming in the music industry, is going to alleviate that in terms of privacy of consumer data.”

Businesses will need to be transparent about their data practices and comply with regulations such as the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation, which protects consumer data across the EU.

Engaging with AI technologies includes balancing the benefits with protection against misuse or unethical practices.

“Your data is already out there; what AI is changing is simply the sophistication with which your data is being used,” says Inge.

### Bias in algorithms

AI models are trained on data sets to recognize certain patterns or make certain decisions. Training an AI model on data with historical or representational bias could lead to unfair representation or discrimination against certain groups or individuals, eroding trust in AI and damaging the reputations of organizations that use it.

When systems use biased data, it can create a negative feedback loop that reinforces bias over time, repeating the same patterns and increasing skewed results. This is an important consideration for industries such as healthcare, human resources, and finance that are increasingly turning to AI to inform decision-making.

“We have a very long way to go before we start correcting that bias,” Inge says. “It is an absolute concern.”

While anti-discrimination laws in Europe prohibit discrimination in online advertising, it still persists, regardless. To mitigate data bias, companies must audit their systems and ensure representative data sets are used when training algorithmic models. To prevent bias in AI from persisting — or evolving — maintaining this vigilance is crucial.

## Using AI Responsibly

Balancing the benefits of AI with potential negative impacts to consumers and society at large is crucial for ethical AI adoption in marketing.

Marketers should ensure AI systems are transparent and provide clear explanations to consumers on how their data is used and how marketing decisions are made. Informed consumers are more likely to build trust and comfort with AI use in marketing.

### Tips for responsible AI use

* **Be transparent** The CEO of “Sports Illustrated” magazine was fired in the wake of an AI scandal, after it was revealed the magazine was using AI-generated content without disclosing it to their readers. The problem wasn’t necessarily the use of AI, but the undisclosed nature of its use.
* **Prioritize human oversight** Marketers are rightfully concerned that AI will eliminate jobs. But, AI will need human oversight and will likely create different jobs. AI needs humans to figure out whether or not the information it generates is accurate, and correct mistakes as they occur.
* **Seek customer feedback** In addition to disclosing the use of AI, companies need to provide channels for customer feedback to correct inaccuracies or express discomfort from AI interactions. This will help marketers deliver an experience customers will find trustworthy and helpful.

## **Building AI Expertise: The Marketer’s Next Steps**

To build AI expertise, Inge recommends experimenting with tools that are already available.

“This will help marketers understand their capabilities and limitations, make marketers more comfortable and adept at incorporating AI into their workflows, and stay up-to-date on trends and development,” she says. “Keep an eye on how AI is impacting various roles and tasks and proactively build your expertise.”

Get started with the following steps:

* **Understand the basics:** Get familiar with the core concepts of AI and machine learning
* **Gain hands-on experience:** Work on projects that use data analysis and AI applications
* **Collaborate with data teams:** Learn how to use AI tools for content strategy and search engine optimization
* **Build your portfolio:** Demonstrate your AI expertise by showcasing projects

### Develop your skills

To better target marketing efforts, enhance customer engagement and conversion rates, professionals must be AI literate.

Learning how AI works and understanding safe, ethical, and responsible best practices is crucial to success in using the technology in marketing.

Professionals can gain a competitive advantage by mastering predictive analytics, generative AI, and marketing automation. Additionally, it is crucial to stay up to date with the latest developments by [reskilling](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/blog/how-to-keep-up-with-ai-through-reskilling/), ensuring increased career longevity.

## Focus your learning

* **Targeting:** Learn how to leverage AI to enhance consumer engagements and conversion rates
* **Data-driven insights:** Understand how AI systems use data so you can spot AI bias and resolve it
* **Automation:** Streamline processes so you can focus on strategy, leading to increased efficiency and productivity
* **Generative AI:** Learn how to find innovative solutions and methodologies for data analysis and customer engagement
* **Ethics:** Understand concerns regarding privacy and bias; crucial for responsible marketing practice

Professional and Executive Development offers programs to help professionals develop AI skills. In the [AI for Marketing Course: Transforming Strategies with Generative AI](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/programs/ai-marketing-course/), professionals learn to harness generative AI, hyper-personalization, and predictive analytics to optimize customer engagement, boost conversions, and drive growth.

### Organizational readiness

The 2024 State of AI in Marketing: Key Insights and Future Trends report paints a picture of a marketing industry in transition.

While AI adoption is accelerating, it finds a significant gap between individual enthusiasm for AI and organizational readiness. To bridge the gap, organizations will need to invest in educating their workforce, developing policies and guidelines, and creating a roadmap for implementation.

Companies will need to embrace experimentation, test new ideas, and risk failure to drive innovation.

## AI Programs for Marketers

Organizations that equip their marketing leaders with skills in AI technology will gain a significant competitive edge over the competition.

The two-day [Transforming Strategies with Generative AI](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/programs/ai-marketing-course/) Professional & Executive Development program will prepare professionals to lead AI-driven marketing efforts, leveraging cutting-edge AI tools such as hyper-personalization, predictive insights, and content automation. Through real-world applications, participants will gain hands-on training in the use of this technology and have the opportunity to network with industry leaders and peers.

“Whether it’s analytics, design, brand strategy, [creative direction](https://professional.dce.harvard.edu/blog/how-to-implement-creative-marketing-strategies-at-your-organization/) or copywriting, this course will help with any marketing job,” Inge says. “Participants will understand the current landscape, understand what AI can and cannot do effectively, and then learn to use AI tools to future proof their careers.”

As artificial intelligence changes the marketing industry, the value of AI skills and expertise will only grow, bringing success to those who master them.

# AI in Digital Marketing: What to Expect in 2025

Written by:


Power Digital
Growth Marketing Partner

Power Digital is a full-service growth marketing agency helping brands accelerate their revenue with data, strategy, and execution. Known for our award-winning teams and nova technology, we bring clarity to complexity and build marketing that scales.

It’s on the tip of everyone’s tongue—and it’s the top result in their internet search history: AI is officially here to stay (and grow) in 2025.

One industry benefiting most from the AI tide? Digital marketing. 

AI continues to transform digital marketing by enhancing automation, personalization, and data-driven decision-making. To stay ahead, brands must do more than hop on the bandwagon—they need to lead the revolution. 

From hyper-personalization to generative ad materials and predictive analytics, explore the increasingly significant role of AI in digital marketing and improving customer experiences in 2025.

## **The evolving role of AI in digital marketing**

In 2025, the international AI market is currently valued at over $757 billion—and it’s projected to grow steadily through the decade, with an estimated value of $3.68 trillion by 2030. That’s right—*trillion*. 

While AI is used for everything from translation to animation, it holds massive potential for digital marketing.

AI can do much more than convert text to speech and generate content ideas. According to a HubSpot survey exploring how AI is changing marketing, digital marketers are using generative AI to automate and streamline:

* Content creation.
* Market research.
* Deep learning.
* Data analysis.
* And much more.

In 2025 and beyond, these AI evolutions will allow brands to create predictable growth and explore new marketing horizons. And, staying in line with Darwin, brands will need to evolve with AI to thrive. 

## **Top AI trends shaping digital marketing in 2025**

Here are the most influential AI trends in 2025 that marketers need to watch:

* **Hyper-personalization** – Consumers hunger for highly personalized brand experiences that speak to their wants and needs. In fact, 71% expect personalization, and 76% feel frustrated without it. AI tools now allow marketers to “read consumers’ minds,” tailoring ad campaigns and promotions to each consumer’s unique preferences and behaviors—even ones they aren’t aware of yet.
* **Conversational AI and chatbots** – One essential aspect of personalization is quality customer service. 2025 will see a rise in advanced AI-powered chatbots providing seamless customer service and real-time interactions.
* **AI-powered SEO and content optimization** – Marketers use AI tools like ChatGPT to generate content ideas and materials. Now, they’re enlisting AI to *optimize* that content for enhanced search performance and engagement. These innovative tools offer automated content strategies and real-time search trend adaptation.
* **AI-driven social media marketing** – Digital marketers strive to reach as many consumers in their target audience as possible. And as of 2025, 5.24 billion of those potential consumers are on social media. This staggering number represents lots of eyes—and plenty of noise. With AI-driven predictive analytics for viral trends, engagement optimization, and sentiment analysis, however, brands can craft compelling content that cuts through that noise and resonates with social media users.
* **Voice search and AI-powered assistants** – With the immense volume of products and media available, consumers increasingly desire intuitive search tools and recommendations. With voice search and AI assistants, they can circumvent the search bar for a more natural route to discovering new things. AI will also help brands optimize their marketing strategies for voice-based queries.

## **The future of AI in paid advertising**

Brands are actively learning how to use AI for marketing in all its facets—including paid advertising. Currently, AI is reshaping digital advertising through:

* **Programmatic ad buying** – Gone are the days of billboard and magazine advertising, tossing campaigns out to see if they’ll stick. Now, digital marketers can buy ads with the guarantee that the right eyes will see them. AI-driven ad placements now allow for real-time bidding and optimized targeting, with valuable performance insights to boot.
* **Predictive analytics in ad campaigns** – Another pitfall of the advertising of yore: lack of foresight. With AI’s psychic-like consumer behavior anticipation and ad refining strategies, brands can eliminate guesswork and spend more time and resources creating compelling campaigns that will lead to predictable growth.
* **Automated ad creatives** – AI has transformed time-honored advertising strategies like A/B testing—a method of comparing ad variations that goes back to the 1920s. Marketers can now efficiently create ad variations tailored to each audience segment and automatically track and analyze their performance for enhanced optimization.

## **AI’s role in content creation and marketing automation**

AI tools like ChatGPT and MidJourney brighten internet users’ lives with their fake movie scripts and surreal memes—but they can actually improve the lives of digital marketers, too. Here’s how:

* **Generating compelling copy** – Marketers leverage AI for everything from blog writing to product descriptions and ad creatives. Implement AI into any part of the creative strategy—brainstorming, writing, targeting, performance analysis, and beyond.
* **Automating email marketing** – Remember: Personalization makes for happy customers. AI enhances email tailoring with automated subject line optimization and relevant email sequencing that drives engagement and boosts conversions.
* **Instantly creating videos and images** – As visual social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram continue to grow, so does the need for visual content. And as brands plan to invest more in short-form video and image creation in 2025, marketers can lean on AI to automate creative processes and produce engaging multimedia content.

## **AI in customer experience and retention**

Beyond the endless strategizing and analyzing lies one person that matters above all else: the consumer. AI can help brands find their target consumers, understand them, and connect with them on a deeper level. 

AI’s key brand-consumer matchmaking services include:

* **Behavior-based personalization** – The more marketers know about their target consumers’ online behaviors, the easier it is to deliver personally relevant and meaningful customer experiences. AI-driven recommendations make for even higher retention rates.
* **AI-powered customer support** – Consumers crave real-time support—but when a company reaches a certain scale, manual human interactions can only go so far. AI chatbots and assistants can pick up the slack, providing consumers with valuable help while improving customer service efficiency.
* **Sentiment analysis** – Marketers have access to increasingly vast amounts of consumer data—with no way to wade through it all on their own. AI tools that analyze consumer sentiments and opinions allow marketers to track and respond to feedback with heightened confidence and lightning speed.

## **AI and the future of data privacy and ethics**

All innovations must strike a balance with social well-being—AI is no exception. Brands beginning to integrate AI into their digital marketing strategies should also work to:

* **Protect consumer data** – According to a large-scale 2023 survey, 86% of Americans are concerned about their data security—and 64% believe companies are responsible for protecting it. Since AI in digital marketing relies on consumer data, this responsibility is more important than ever. When using AI, always adhere to any state and federal data privacy laws (and in some cases, the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation). Start by asking for permission!
* **Consider AI bias and ethical practices** – While AI itself isn’t capable of human bias, it relies on consumer data that is. This bias can impact AI-generated recommendations and automated consumer interactions, spelling trouble for brands striving to follow fair marketing practices. Instead of relying on AI for final marketing materials, use it as an initial generation tool and comb through its outputs with an eye trained in human sensitivity.
* **Create transparency in AI-driven marketing** – Half of a brand’s data privacy responsibility is protection—the other is education. Go above and beyond AI ethical practices by being fully transparent about AI usage, including AI-generated content, recommendations, and automated decision-making.

## **How businesses can prepare for AI in 2025**

Many industry professionals are asking, “Will digital marketing be replaced by AI?” This line of thought highlights a key misunderstanding of AI’s capabilities. With a robust AI strategy, brands will be able to *enhance* their digital marketing efforts—not replace them. 

Marketers looking to integrate AI into their strategies can take action by:

* **Investing in AI tech** – From generative applications like ChatGPT and Grammarly to analytic platforms SEMRush and Brandwatch, there are many AI tools designed to optimize specific tasks. Marketers should do research to find the AI-powered marketing tools and automation platforms that will best support their team’s needs and goals.
* **Building AI skills** – AI is not an extra digital marketing team member—it’s a tool for marketing teams to benefit from. Enhancing team skills in AI-driven analytics and marketing technologies will boost impact and return on investment (ROI).
* **Adapting marketing strategies** – According to Hubspot, digital marketers are excited about the new potential of AI tools—but fewer than 50% feel confident implementing AI into their current strategy and measuring its impact. Learn to adapt strategies to accommodate new tools and leverage AI for improved efficiency and engagement.

The 2025 AI wave is still cresting—digital marketers should be prepared to hop on their surfboard and ride it. 

## **The future of AI-driven digital marketing**

Digital marketers have an important job: Connecting with consumers and driving action, one eye always trained on growth. In 2025, AI will be the key to shaping data-driven, consumer-centric marketing strategies that allow businesses to scale faster and greater than ever before. 

Stay ahead by embracing AI innovations and refining your own digital marketing approaches for 2025 and beyond.
